Golden Scenarios and Prototype Acceptance Tests

Status: Vision validation scenarios, not a production schedule \| 22 November 2026

# How to use

These scenarios test whether the game feels like Irreverents. They are intentionally cross-system and behavior-centered, not precise engineering tasks. “Success” is qualitative player experience plus consistent world behavior. Designers may invent different places/characters to prove the same point.

# G-01 The room nobody will listen in

Setup: royal court with king giving an important briefing, visible curious objects and NPCs.

Experience: player can freely explore while king talks; the easiest way to progress is to act rather than politely wait; king reacts to disruption.

Variants: peaceful exit, theft, king/champion fight, monster release, secret route.

Pass: no forced expo gate; player agency meaningful in first minute.

# G-02 Most patient hero

Setup: king continues oration.

Experience: player waits approximately three hours and speech seamlessly becomes actual credits.

Pass: valid, discoverable, surprising alternate end without leaving starting room. No short obvious loops.

# G-03 Return with a new character

Setup: early forest area with high canopy, narrow route and stone barrier.

Experience: long after first arrival, newly recruited character unlocks a deep secret and a shortcut.

Pass: revisiting feels like rediscovery, not backtracking for an icon collectible.

# G-04 The honest co-op gate

Setup: two mechanisms need simultaneous sustained actuation.

Experience: two humans solve by coordinating powers. Solo player is not hard-blocked by player count and may discover physical workaround.

Pass: world rules remain consistent whether solution was predicted or not.

# G-05 The zero-alarm heist

Setup: guarded jewel vault with layered patrols, multiple routes and a legitimate treasure.

Experience: party steals objective, slips out and triggers no alarms.

Pass: stealth is flexible, understandable, strategically gratifying and recognized as a potentially legendary achievement.

# G-06 The heist catastrophe

Setup: same vault.

Experience: a single mistake triggers alarms; group fights enormous reinforcements, steals a security vehicle, smashes through walls or finds a hiding route.

Pass: players keep playing because the combat/escape is so entertaining; alarm is not a soft failure state.

# G-07 The unbeatable crowd

Setup: party against many ordinary guards and some strong elites.

Experience: repeated spectacular launches, throws into other opponents, collapsing objects, increasing numbers; eventual defeat or rare survival.

Pass: highly powerful moment-to-moment action even when eventual loss is inevitable.

# G-08 The roadblock

Setup: commandeered machine moving at speed toward enemy barricade.

Experience: hit has buildup, impact and consequence: debris, defenders launched, mass visible, controls recover.

Pass: player says “OHH!” without relying on giant text damage numbers or cinematic override.

# G-09 Steal the response itself

Setup: escalating guards dispatch their strongest machine to stop party.

Experience: clever players capture it and turn it on pursuing troops.

Pass: extraordinary emergent reversal is supported by mechanical rules, not a pre-scripted mission flag.

# G-10 Provocation and cooling down

Setup: otherwise friendly inhabited town, NPCs with varying behaviors.

Experience: start bar fight or steal vehicle; pursue until hidden; search gradually cools; reenter town.

Pass: enough reaction to feel alive, enough recovery to make experimentation inviting.

# G-11 The dragon-cloak-town-arena saga

Setup: same world systems: dragon crisis, grateful town, stealth reward, jewel treasure, nearby arena and undead.

Experience: party may create unexpected rescue–betrayal–chase–alliance chain; NPCs remember contradictory feelings.

Pass: result is coherent even if gameplay takes a different path, not a rigid mandatory cutscene.

# G-12 A legend belongs to its participants

Setup: online party finishes extraordinary zero-alarm stealth or overwhelming battle; includes a player from another world/session.

Experience: all participants receive a record with screenshot and contextual stats.

Pass: nobody is excluded due to not having initiated or landed final hit; event remains accessible after session.

# G-13 The Hall commemorates itself

Setup: party visits Hall of Legends.

Experience: provoke guards, steal an artifact, hijack a defender, trigger museum battle, escape or die; a framed record memorializes that event in the same Hall.

Pass: Hall obeys world rules, survives as historical record, can recursively depict an earlier monument.

# G-14 The irresistible diversion

Setup: clear quest marker toward ancient world-saving crisis; nearby strange creature, sealed passage and compelling vehicle.

Experience: players pursue distractions for hours without being punished into main quest.

Pass: the diversions are genuinely deep, memorable, mechanically rich, not just shallow collectibles.

# G-15 Same power, multiple meanings

Setup: one ability (e.g., suplex, wind or ice) appears in combat, traversal, puzzle and stealth contexts.

Experience: players recognize and improvise with its consistent affordances.

Pass: at least one surprising usage is not explicitly tutorialized.

# G-16 Regeneration without erasure

Setup: party destroys a major public area and eventually leaves.

Experience: world records/social memory and the Hall can commemorate catastrophe while essential navigation/content remains viable.

Pass: neither meaningless instant reset nor permanent broken save.

# Early vertical slice hypothesis

A compact explorable castle-town/royal audience and connected secret undercroft could demonstrate: single shared party, 2–3 character functions, one or two acquirable powers, a quiet heist, dynamic guard reaction, high-impact grab/throw, one hijackable response vehicle, an escape route, and an event memorial. This is an illustrative recommended vertical slice, not a project-owner-approved production scope.

# Evaluation questions for playtests

What was the most memorable unplanned event? Did a player experiment without being prompted? Could they return to exploration after chaos? Did enemy impacts feel weighty? Was retreat fun even when hope was small? Did discovering a new character cause immediate curiosity about old regions? Did any co-op puzzle feel arbitrary? Did the Hall's record seem earned and faithful to what happened?
